recipes.name: Grilled Portobello with Basil Mayonnaise Sandwich
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon butter, softened, or as needed

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Whisk vinegar, oil, and garlic together in a small bowl.
Arrange mushrooms on a baking sheet with the gills facing up; brush with about 2/3 of the marinade and let sit for 3 to 5 minutes.
Transfer mushrooms to the preheated grill with the gills facing down; grill, basting occasionally with remaining marinade, until tender, about 4 minutes per side.
While the mushrooms are cooking, mix mayonnaise, basil, Dijon, and lemon juice together in a small bowl. Butter toasted rolls, then spread with mayonnaise mixture.
Remove mushrooms from the grill and place on bottom buns. Top with lettuce, tomatoes, and top buns.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Portobello with Basil Mayonnaise Sandwich
raw_recipe.description: Grilled portobello sandwich with lettuce, tomato, and basil mayo on a bulky kaiser roll — perfect for lunch on a summer day.

review.reviewBody: I've made this recipe several times already this summer, and it is delicious! The only change I made was not buttering the buns, and toasting them on the grill. The mayo combo is so good, I use it on other veggie sandwiches. Thanks for the great recipe.

I used this recipe, but I only made 2 extra large mushrooms since I'm the only fan. I used 1/2 tsp. dried basil because that's what I had on hand, and I made it on my stove top grill pan. Since I'm doing the keto diet, I put one atop a low carb fajita with the mayo, tomato, and lettuce and ate it like an open-faced sandwich, sloppy but all the flavors were there. I plan to use the leftover marinade and mayo with some leftover sliced steak on a fajita. I will make this again.

This was unbelievable. I was concerned that the texture would be weird but it was perfect. I added tarragon to the mix because that’s one of my favorite herbs. I also used some of the mayonnaise mixture (instead of butter) on the buns before browning in a pan. I find using mayonnaise helps so much with the flavor. I used baby spinach, red onions, tomato and slivers of Asiago cheese. I will be making this many more times.

We LOVED this “burger!” My husband has never had a portobello mushroom burger so he wasn’t very excited for the menu tonight but absolutely loved the result. We followed the recipe exactly except we never flipped the mushroom or put gill-side down. Instead; we grilled a little longer and not over direct heat. This left the juice/marinade remain on the mushroom while grilling. We did toast the buns and added a slice of provolone over the mushrooms during the last minute of cooking to melt. With the Basil Mayo, tomato, lettuce…yum!!! Do not put onto buns until ready to eat or your buns will get a little soggy; which I didn’t mind but I could see impact to presentation & texture. Absolutely awesome and already planning to make again THIS WEEK!! Thank you!!!

Absolutley loved this one! I bought 2 huge portobello mushrooms to grill. The basil mayo rocks out....I used low fat mayo and fresh lemon juice and fresh basil....which I always think is key to get the best flavors....I served on a whole wheat sandwich thin (Arnold brand). Nice summer dinner! Thanks!

This was amazing! I have made marinated portobellos before, and the vinegar was overwhelming - this was just right! I marinated the portobellos for an hour, then pan-fried them with 1 Tbl. olive oil (covered) for about 6 minutes on each side, then sprinkled with a little bit of salt. I left off the butter on the rolls because I didn't think it was necessary (and is just added fat). The basil-mayonnaise was the perfect touch. Thanks for the recipe!

Delicious! Very satisfying on a hot summer night. The only changes I made were 1) to marinade the mushrooms in the vinegar/oil/garlic for 2 hours instead of just brushing it on before grilling. The mushrooms were very flavorful that way, and 2) to add a slight amount of cheese (pick your favorite) onto the mushrooms just before taking off the grill. I loved the mayo, and will look for other ways to use it!
This was great! Made no changes just additions, we added fresh mozzarella slices, warmed roasted peppers and grilled asparagus and red onion. Even my skeptical husband enjoyed it!

WOW - these are fabulous! I love portobello mushrooms, so I had to give this a try. Plus they're so easy to put together. It's great for lunch or a quick weeknight meal. I would recommend marinating the mushrooms for a couple of hours vs. a few minutes. Don't skip the basil mayo, it's awesome! I used Hellman's light mayo and toasted some sesame seed rolls then added a slice of provolone along with the rest of the ingredients. These are so good, you'll never miss the meat!

Wow, so good! I added a bit of minced garlic to the mayo mixture, skipped grilling the buns and subbed roasted red peppers and mozzarella for the lettuce and tomato. Couldn't believe what a quick and delicious meal this was - thanks!

I used portobello mushrooms as big as a kaiser bun. I took the stems off and then marinaded them all day, gill side up, to soak in the marinade. 
I didn't use garlic and I didn't butter the buns.
I followed the rest of the recipe. They were delicious. The basil mayo really compliments the marinaded mushroom flavor.
This is my favorite portobello mushroom recipe! The flavors are delicious, and people always want more.
I made these mushrooms with ciabatta rolls butter-toasted on the grill, roasted red peppers, slice of provolone and arugula. Add the basil mayo and you are in for a gourmet-tasting treat!

Just finished and shocked at how good it was! First time trying a plant burger and fully expected NOT to like it but what a delicious surprise! I can easily make this my burger go-to. I'm still licking my chops. Will be sharing this to all who will listen. Only addition was to zest lemon into the sauce and it brightened things up.
I have loved this recipes for years. The basil mayo is the star. Healthy and delicious...what's not to love?
I did enjoy these grilled mushroom burgers. A great, filling meat substitute. However, the recipe does not produce enough of the basil mayonnaise for the amount of sandwiches it makes.
We tried this for one of our meatless meals and it was delish! We love mushrooms but the basil sauce was the finishing touch. Will definitely be making again@
This was delicious! We used small buns so there was less bread. Super good!!!!
